stage1.impression: A competent but plainly CG back-bar: the bright, neutral-white lit shelf edges read as LED strips in a nightclub or a liquor-store display, and the niche reads as a lit display case, so the speaker looks more like a product in a showroom than furniture in a room. The fir counter takes the bottom third and is a smooth, dull brown plane with no pool of light on it. The near glass is a blurred white block. The bottles are obvious repeats, the concrete has no board-form character at this scale, and the frame is darker than a published night interior (median 17).

blocking_9: Lit shelf edges warm (about 2400 to 2700 K) and secondary, not the brightest neutral-white lines in the frame
Frame lum_median 24 to 40, with shadows that hold detail in the back-bar and the counter
A visible pool of pendant light on the fir counter, falling off naturally toward the camera
The Fog speaker reads at a glance as thick clear acrylic over white batts, with glowing edges and clean reflections, not a white box in a lit case
The near glass reads as a real rocks glass with liquid, ice or a believable highlight, plus at least one more sign of life (a record sleeve, a menu)
Bottles varied in shape, height, label and fill, with no repeated model visible
Concrete showing board-form grain, pour lines or tie holes at 1:1
Some atmosphere: faint visible haze in the niche spots' beams

defects.what: Shelf lit edges are near-white (lum_median 184, R194 G182 B177) against a 2400 K room: they read as LED strip signage and pull the eye from the speaker
Same white LED-strip edges on the right-hand shelves
Niche back is a flat, evenly lit grey field behind the upper cabinet: reads as a display case or lightbox
White batts and woofer area are hot (lum_p95 228); the lower cabinet reads as a white box, and the acrylic's edges and thickness barely register
Near glass is a defocused white rectangle (crush 5.6 %, p95 175); it does not read as glass
Counter is a smooth, uniform dark plane (lum_median 26, range 35) with no pool of light and little grain; the front edge is mushy
Repeated bottle models with identical labels, a CG giveaway
Concrete behind the shelves is a mottled dark texture with no formwork boards, pour lines or tie holes
Pendant's frosted tube is cool white (B200 > R196) and clipping (3.5 %), so it does not match the warm room
Labels and wall show denoiser smear; there is no visible haze (density 0.008)

changes.problem: The shelves' lit edges are the brightest, coolest lines in the frame and read as nightclub LED strips.

evidence.measured: lum_median 184.3, R194 G182 B177 (neutral white in a 2400 K room)

change.setting: the shelves' lit edges (emission strength and colour)

changes.expected: The edges glow as warm, polished acrylic edges that sit under the speaker in the hierarchy, and the bottles pick up warm rim light.

changes.problem: The frame is too dark for a published night interior; the back-bar's shadows are nearly empty.

change.to: 1.1 (after c1 and c3 have removed the hot whites)

changes.expected: Frame median in the high 20s to low 30s, with the bottles, the concrete and the counter's grain readable.

changes.problem: The niche is lit like a display case: a flat grey back and 300 W spots blow the batts to white, so the clear acrylic's thickness and edges are lost.

evidence.measured: lum_median 141, lum_p95 228; backdrop at [330,125,445,250] lum_median 52, flat

change.setting: in each niche 2 x spot (power) and the niches' frosted backs
change.to: 160 W, 2600 K, aimed to graze the cabinet's sides from above so the acrylic edges catch light; frosted back 0.12 with a top-to-bottom falloff

changes.expected: The speaker reads as a glowing clear block with bright edges against a darker, graded niche. The batts are bright but not glaring.

changes.problem: The fir counter takes a third of the frame but has no pool of light, so it reads as a flat dark plane.

evidence.measured: lum_median 34.4; y-profile of [0,330,720,480] 28-34-19 with no defined pool

change.setting: pendants 3 x spot (power, cone) and the fir's finish
change.to: 110 W, cone 35 deg, with the nearest pendant's pool on the counter just left of the glass; fir finish a little glossier (oiled), so the pool shows grain and a soft sheen

changes.expected: A warm oval pool on the counter that falls to dark toward the lens and the edges, with the grain legible inside it.

changes.problem: The near glass is a blurred white block, and the frame has no sign of life.

evidence.measured: white rectangular highlight, p95 175, crush 5.6 %, edge width 16 px (defocused)

change.from: empty glass at the near edge, out of focus
change.to: a heavy-based rocks glass with two fingers of whisky and one large clear ice cube, moved about 25 cm farther in so it falls inside the depth of field (or f/2.8 to f/4), plus a record sleeve leaning on the counter and a folded menu

changes.expected: The glass reads as glass: an amber body, a caustic on the counter, and a small specular highlight instead of a white slab.

changes.problem: The back-bar bottles are visibly the same few models with identical labels.

evidence.measured: seen: matching label bands and silhouettes repeat across shelves

change.to: at least 12 distinct shapes and heights, labels varied in tone and size, fill levels from 20 to 100 %, some smoked or green glass, spacing irregular, a few bottles turned

changes.expected: The shelves read as a working bar's stock, not an asset scatter.

changes.problem: The pendant at the top right is cool white and clipping, which breaks the single warm set of practicals.

change.setting: the pendants' frosted tubes and lamps (emission)

changes.expected: The frosted tube glows warm and even, with no clipped area.

changes.problem: There is no atmosphere: the dark areas are empty and the beams are invisible.

evidence.measured: lum_p5 7.8; no visible beam from the niche or pendant spots

changes.expected: The spots draw faint cones, and the shadows lift slightly while keeping their depth.

out_of_scope.request: Make the Fog speaker read as the frame's one colour (a tint)
out_of_scope.why: The card fixes it as water-clear acrylic over white batts. Its presence has to come from light (c3), not colour.

out_of_scope.request: Show the concrete's board-form grain, pour lines and tie holes
out_of_scope.why: This is a material-texture change (the scale and relief of the board marks). The card allows the concrete's tone and sheen but not its texture. It is a blocker for a 9, so the owner or modeller should decide.
The shelves' thickness and mounting belong to the back-bar's design, which the card fixes.
